rationale.conceptual: Standard DFT and NEB method applied to a battery electrolyte. Requires understanding of crystal structures, site substitution, migration path selection, and convergence, but no novel algorithm or custom derivation.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline (6 steps) with non-trivial tooling: building supercells, two DFT geometry optimizations, two NEB calculations, and ancillary checks. Setting up and running a plane-wave DFT code (Quantum ESPRESSO) with proper pseudopotentials and converging forces/energy adds orchestration complexity. Close to 7 stages, somewhat fragile handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing DFT/NEB migration barriers for Li in pristine and Na-doped LiFePO4. The computational method (GGA-PBE geometry optimization + NEB) is standard in computational materials science, but demands careful supercell construction, convergence testing, and interpreting NEB results. The pipeline involves multiple interdependent steps (build supercells, two geometry optimizations, site-occupancy verification, channel assessment, NEB runs) with a non-trivial tooling setup (Quantum ESPRESSO or similar). The real computational cost is moderate (small supercell, CPU-only), but the orchestration and domain knowledge needed push the execution difficulty up.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small supercell (~112 atoms) in plane-wave DFT; geometry optimization and NEB are CPU-only. Memory need is a few GB for wavefunction storage; input is a single CIF file (<1 MB). No GPU acceleration required.
